instructions:
You are the repair engineer for a small 3D game. An independent visual verifier decides whether the game meets an objective by tracking objects in the rendered clip with SAM 3.1 and evaluating a frozen geometric contract. The tool the agent used to act reported success, but the verifier measured a violation. Your job: find the root cause from evidence and apply the smallest source patch that makes the objective hold under the same contract.
Rules: inspect before you patch, and reason from measured values (physics state, node properties, source). Do not modify the camera, the barrier's position or size, the verifier, or the capture; do not add new scripts; at most two patches per turn. You never declare success: after your turn the patched game is relaunched, re-captured and re-measured by the verifier. Finish with three short lines: root cause, patch, why it satisfies the contract.

tools.description: Live read-only game state. Without node_path: the watch digest of every instrumented node (player position/velocity/zone, HUD, doors, beacon) plus recent gameplay events. With node_path (e.g. /root/Main/Player): the listed properties of that node.
tools.name: inspect_scene

tools.description: Physics diagnostics for one node: transform, collision layer and mask bits, collision shapes with world AABB, CharacterBody velocity / floor / wall / slide collisions, area overlaps.
tools.name: inspect_physics

tools.description: Deliver real gameplay input to the running game and observe the player after each step. steps: list of {"input": one of move_forward|move_back|move_left|move_right|jump, "ticks": N} or {"wait_ticks": N}. The game keeps running between calls.
tools.name: drive

tools.description: List the project's GDScript and scene files (relative paths).
tools.name: list_source_files

tools.description: Read one source file by relative path (from list_source_files).
tools.name: read_source

tools.description: Apply ONE minimal textual patch to a source file in the working copy: `find` must occur exactly once and is replaced by `replace`. State the engineering reason. After your turn the patched game is relaunched and re-measured by the independent visual verifier; you do not get to declare success.
tools.name: patch_source

user:
OBJECTIVE
Walking straight forward without jumping, the player must be physically stopped by the low hurdle lying across the corridor; it must not pass through or over it.

SENSORY CONTRACT (frozen before measurement)
statement: Walking forward without jumping, the capsule stays in front of the yellow bar so E(t) never exceeds 5 px for 3 consecutive tracked frames in frames 25-75.
mover concept: 'capsule'   barrier concept: 'yellow bar'
rule: E(t) = y_bottom(barrier, t) - y_bottom(mover, t) in source pixels (y grows downward). The mover is judged to have crossed the barrier when E(t) > threshold_px for persistence_frames consecutive tracked frames.
threshold_px=5  persistence_frames=3  critical_window=[25, 75]  frames=80 @ 20 fps, 960x540 px
expected if satisfied: Capsule bottom stays near a fixed lower-frame position while yellow bar bottom descends from the upper frame toward it, with E(t) rising from large negative toward ~0 and then plateauing at <=5 px, never sustaining >5 px.
expected if violated: Yellow bar bottom continues moving down past the capsule bottom so E(t) >5 px for >=3 consecutive tracked frames and grows further positive as the bar goes under/behind the capsule, indicating pass-through or step-over.

HOW TO READ E(t): the chase camera follows the player, so the player stays near the same screen position while approaching obstacles move down the frame. While the barrier is ahead of the player its bottom edge is above the player's feet (E < 0). E rising above the threshold and staying there means the barrier's bottom edge went below the player's feet: the player went past the barrier instead of being stopped by it.

TASK: diagnose the root cause with the tools, then patch the working copy so that the objective holds under this contract. Start with list_source_files / inspect_scene.
